analysis:
Examined the new ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift (head, lines 1-388) and the ProviderLoop+Serve.swift shutdown changes (patch at ~497 and ~523, with base context).

The new recovery loop re-loads operator-selected models that the startup preload skipped or that Autopilot unloaded. It runs on the capacity tick. It may evict only models outside the selection, via unloadModel(forEviction: true). Eviction is gated by isProtectedFromRecoveryEviction, evictionExclusions, Autopilot victim-wait rules and a recheck immediately before each unload. It pauses while draining, updating, reconnecting after retirement, under a live Autopilot lease, during a model switch, during startup preload, or during any other load or unload. The load uses ensureModelLoaded(allowEviction: false), which goes through the existing load gate.

This touches no encryption, attestation, coordinator authorization, or consumer data paths. The affected assets are A-018 and the TB-007 inference-engine availability. The recovery state is local. It is fed by operator config and Autopilot state, not by untrusted remote input, apart from the existing coordinator-driven Autopilot commands. Those were already handled by the Autopilot control path. The only new influence is that noteSelectedModelUnloaded enqueues victims, and that requires the target to be an explicitly selected, advertised, eligible, unfenced model.

Shutdown: the in-flight recovery attempt task is added to the preloads that get cancelled and awaited, with the existing timeout. The inline unload loop is replaced by unloadAllModelsForShutdown(). That function is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that it preserves the old semantics: waiting for pending unloads and repeating until modelSlots is empty. I could not confirm it still waits out any recovery attempt that outlives the preload timeout. Because the recovery task has a guard on isShuttingDown and Task.isCancelled, a late load seems unlikely, but it is unverified. I raise no finding because there is no evidence of a regression.

Other unverified contracts: the SelectedModelRecovery state type, enqueue/backoff behavior, DaemonState report fields (no secrets, only model ids and timing), and the call sites that enqueue from finishStartupPreload.

No security regression identified. A light follow-up should confirm the unloadAllModelsForShutdown semantics.
